m1.quote: Bundling all of them into a single Go binary/service is a huge maintenance and security surface for what appears to be a small team, and it raises the classic "does one thing well vs. does everything adequately" question.
m1.note: Asserts small team plus broad security surface implies inadequately maintained/battle-tested security-critical components like the OAuth server.

m2.quote: Each one of these (an OAuth server, a BI-style portal, a semantic gateway) is normally its own project.
m2.note: Treats the built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization server as home-grown auth that is a maturity/security red flag rather than delegated identity.

m3.note: Engages directly with the benchmark and DOI-archived report, criticizing it as self-produced and narrow rather than absent.

m4.note: Correctly acknowledges the PostgreSQL-only fallback and limits the DataHub requirement to the cross-enrichment feature.
